title: Sharpeville massacre
summary: On 21 March 1960 police opened fire on a crowd gathered at the Sharpeville police station, south of Johannesburg, during a Pan Africanist Congress protest against the pass laws. The official inquest counted 69 dead and 180 seriously wounded; other sources give 180 to over 200 injured. The killings drew UN condemnation and led to a state of emergency and bans on the ANC and PAC.

uncertainty.note: Date agrees across opened pages. Injury figures differ: 180 seriously wounded (official inquest, per SAHO), more than 180 injured (Canadian Museum for Human Rights).

where.modern_name: Sharpeville, near Vereeniging, Gauteng, South Africa
where.historical_name: Sharpeville, a Black township near Vereeniging, Transvaal Province, Union of South Africa

importance.justification: Turning point in the anti-apartheid struggle, marked each year by the UN on 21 March.

audience_note: Describes a police shooting of unarmed protesters, most hit as they fled. Casualty figures are contested.

related.because: The pass laws protested at Sharpeville were part of the apartheid system built after 1948.

sources.title: International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination, 21 March

reviewer_note: 69 dead in every source; wounded given as 180 seriously wounded (SAHO, citing the official inquest) and more than 180 (CMHR). Banning of ANC/PAC is 7 April 1960 in SAHO but 8 April in CMHR; SAHO used. Crowd size also varies by source.

beats.caption: Police fired on a pass-law protest at Sharpeville; the official inquest counted 69 dead and 180 seriously wounded.
The government banned the ANC and PAC under the Unlawful Organisations Act, after declaring a state of emergency.
